A cycle-rickshaw with a big brass loudspeaker horn parked by a striped canvas magic show tent at night in an Indian small town, kerosene lamps, the tent flap open on a lit stage, a clean dusty ground. Painted like a 1960s Indian chromolithograph print for a travelling jadoo show: hand-painted gouache with soft airbrushed glows, saturated vermilion and magenta against a deep indigo night, emerald and old-gold highlights, bold dark outlines, dramatic and mysterious, a little faded, paper grain. Wide panoramic composition: the main subject sits in the left third of the frame. Towards the right the same scene carries on, quieter and darker: open sky, distance and shadow, nothing important there, one continuous picture with no panels and no split. Full-bleed edge to edge, no border, no frame, no people, no faces, no hands. No text, no letters, no numbers, no words, no logos, no badges, no religious symbols, no writing anywhere.
